Source image shows a simple one-diode resistor network with a fixed drop and ideal conducting slope. Two divider cases are standard application, not a nuanced model or several-unit integration.

anchor_interpretation.reasoning: Count dependent solution operations and case branching, not text length or number of options. A direct substitute is1; a gradient-normalization-projection chain is2; several regimes or dependent models is3; multi-stage trajectory/strategy branching is4.
anchor_interpretation.integration: 1 means one topic with related facts;2 means coupled distinct topics;3 means linked major units. No increase merely because a problem is visually busy.
anchor_interpretation.representation: 2 means decoding one topology/transform;3 requires multiple representations/intermediate circuit states, phase geometry, spectral constructions or a generated piecewise curve.
anchor_interpretation.no_equal_count_constraint: Yearly band counts were not normalized. Anchored score comparisons, not expected year rank or quota, determine changes.

residual_subjectivity: Expert-AI estimates are not empirical item difficulty. The same source problem can admit shortcuts; scores target a sound efficient prepared-candidate solution. Adjacent scores near65 should not be treated as a validated categorical discontinuity.
reference_drift_notes: Several other-year anchors assign integration2 to short scalar substitutions or geometry conversions, whereas the strict rubric can read those as one topic plus related facts. Do not raise all own records merely to match annual medians.
A circuit-to-plot transfer problem deserves representation3 only when an intermediate piecewise representation is actually constructed; a printed schematic alone remains1/2.
